In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the covariant density-functional theory is a powerful and reliable tool to investigate nuclear excitations.
the covariant density functionals are able to provide a consistent description of SD excitations not only in the $^{16}$F nucleus but also in the $^{14}$C nucleus.
the fine structure of SD excitation for both $(p, n)$ and $(n, p)$ channels is well understood with a covariant density functional approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the covariant density-functional theory can provide a consistent understanding of the charge-exchange SD excitations in $^{16}O$.
the charge-exchange SD excitations in $^{16}$(O,N) are understood in terms of the covariant density function theory.
the charge-exchange SD excitations are very sensitive to the exchange terms and the fine structures can be used to probe the exchange terms in the nuclear effective interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the charge-exchange spin dipole excitations in $^{16}O$ are very sensitive to the fine details of the nuclear force.

the SD excitations in $^{16}N$ are much weaker than those in $^{16}\text{F}$, which is in sharp contrast to the conventional wisdom that the SD excitation in $^{16}{\rm N}$ should be stronger than that in $^{16\text{F}}$ due to the isovector spin-orbit force.

the SD excitation is not a simple collective mode, but is a complex excitation mode with a rich fine structure, which can be used to probe the detailed structure of the $\sigma$ meson and its coupling to the nucleon.
